### yushin-marshal--queen-sunduk  (Queen Sunduk, 632)
  person=yushin look=marshal from= place=surabol scene=Coronation Morning
  [p] The corridor suddenly remembers it has somewhere else to be.
  [undefined] Tie it tight. If I’m going to be ridiculous, I won’t be late as well.
  [p] One man stays at the door, where a guard would stand if the guard were the most famous swordsman in Silla. Kim Yushin is thirty-seven. He runs the Hwarang yard: horse, bow, gyuku, the place boys learn whether they matter. People call him the Sword of Silla. He is also, everyone notices, very fond of the princess.
  >>> CARD [card yushin:marshal] Thirty-seven. Gaya blood, Silla rank, and the yard is his.
  [undefined] You heard him. / I put on this confident face, but honestly — me, a king… / I’ll do it no matter what. I just don’t know if I can.
  [#4a8fe0] Whether you do it well or badly — / that is what “no matter what” means. / In all this world, wouldn’t it be good to have one person always on your side, Princess? / Hwarang Kim Yushin. / I will serve you to the end.
  [p] She laughs. Nobody else will hear her do that today. Then the bells start.
  [scene] The Palace Road
  FIRST LINES:
    "Whether you do it well or badly — / that is what “no matter what” means. / In all this world, wouldn’t it be good to have one person always on your side, Princess? / Hwarang Kim Yushin. / I will serve you to the end."
    "Slaves, Princess. They aren’t in the count."
    "Are you feeling alright, your majesty?"

  >>> CARD [card munhee] Twenty-six, sharp-tongued, and married to the wrong man on purpose.
  [#e07fa8] Totally unfit for a Noble woman… Come on, boy, can’t you find something better?
  [p] Her husband Chunchu is twenty-nine, and already the most cunning man in Samhan. Only the quiet rooms know it yet.
  [card chunchu:prince] Spring and autumn. Also the name of the oldest chronicle Confucius ever edited. He means to be in the next one.
  [p] Gotaso sits in front of him on the same horse. Bupmin, six, has his own, and will not share the saddle.

### jinheung--jinheung-the-cloud  (Jinheung, the Cloud, 554)
  person=jinheung look= from= place= scene=Coronation Night
  [#8a8a94] Majesty. You wanted the Cloud King. / Everyone loses to him, you know. He’s dead. The dead stop making mistakes.
  [undefined] Then tell me his mistakes. I’ve heard the rest all day.
  [p] He was seven when they put the crown on him. It was too big, and nobody mentioned it. By the end, Silla had a river, a coastline and Gaya. He got there by being the best ally in Samhan, right up until the afternoon he wasn't.
  >>> CARD [card jinheung] The Cloud King. Wherever he rides, the border rides after him.
  [p] He put up stones wherever he stopped — four of them, on mountains, at the edges of what he had taken — and the stones do not boast. They say who came, and when, and that the land is now inside the border. They are property deeds.
  [#8a8a94] There’s no boasting on those stones at all. I’ve read them. I climbed two mountains to do it. / Boasting is for men who are worried about losing it.
  [quote] On the twenty-first day of the eighth month, in the first year of Taechang, the Great King Jinheung toured the lands in his keeping, and had this cut into stone. … And so the borders were carried out 
  [p] Late in his reign he invents the Hwarang. Take the noblest boys and put them in one yard. Make them ride, sing and rank each other until the ranking feels like fate. Nearly every man who matters later comes out of that yard.
  FIRST LINES: (none)

### elderyunbi--eight-great-clans  (Eight Great Clans, 632)
  person=elderyunbi look= from= place= scene=The Sand
  [p] On the crown prince’s day, the court chalks a square grid in the palace yard. Four hard lines. No banners. The young men of each house step onto the grid in white.
  [#8a8a94] The Yunbi boys turned a Satek cart over at the west bridge yesterday. / Then tonight the Satek go over a Yunbi wall. / Same as the lantern festival last year. / Last year three of them died.
  [#d9b13a] White cloth. Wooden swords. / If anyone bleeds the wrong colour, the harbour talks stop for a month.
  >>> CARD [card elderyunbi] Head of the Yunbi. The family business is knowing things first.
  [#c4a35a] Then keep your boys’ wrists honest. / The chalk does not care whose sleeve they hold.
  [p] Swords first. Wooden ones, which still remember steel. The Jinmo boy holds his blade high over his head, the Jinmo way, daring you. A Hae boy takes the dare. On the call they both move. Blades skim the chalk. The white sleeves clap together so close that the steps gasp.
  [#8a8a94] That Jinmo boy? / Fast wrists. / Faster feet than the Hae, too. / Point to Jinmo.
  [p] The Jinmo boy bows to the steps and looks straight past the Hae boy, to the edge of the sand, where the crown prince’s nobody is waiting.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Then keep your boys’ wrists honest. / The chalk does not care whose sleeve they hold."
    "Your boy’s knee touched first. / Ask the chalk."
    "You hold the king’s sleeve and call it a harbour. / We don’t hold the sleeve. We hold the arm."

### gyeonggeunchogo--gunchogo-the-13th  (Gunchogo, the 13th, 371)
  person=gyeonggeunchogo look= from= place= scene=
  [p] Baekje’s thirteenth king marches north to Pyongyang. A Goguryeo king dies on his own wall. In seven hundred years, it never happens again.
  >>> CARD [card gyeonggeunchogo] The king every later Baekje king quotes when he wants to sound brave.
  [place pyongyang]
  [p] Baekje has the river, the coast and the sea roads east. The clans take the docks. The throne takes a cut. It is the richest kingdom in Samhan, and the strongest. Neither lasts.
  [p] What its king wants is the one thing Baekje doesn’t have: the north’s capital. One winter he takes thirty thousand men up the frozen roads to get it.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Good. I’d hate to walk this far for an empty one. / Nobody from the south has ever stood on that wall. Our grandsons will want to know who was first."
    "Then he’s braver than I am, and we’ll find out what that’s worth."
    "That’s a king’s funeral. / …Turn them around. We came for a city. We’re going home with something better."

### gulgul--commander-yeon  (Commander Yeon, 634)

  [p] A month before the summons, in a Mohe village the Eastern Command has finished with, there is a boy who will not move out of the doorway of a house that no longer has a roof. Snow is settling on the ash. He has a shaved crown and two braids, and he holds a stick the way he has seen men hold spears. Yeon gets down off the red bay and walks up until the stick touches his chest.

  person=yeontaejo look= from= place= scene=The Summons

  [p] Back in that first winter, the summons comes. The summons isn't addressed to him. It's addressed to his father, who still holds the Eastern seal. Yeon Taejo sat in the capital's big chair for twelve years. Now he is too old to ride that far. The son has done the work for years. The seal is still the old man's.
  >>> CARD [card yeontaejo] The old Eastern Commander. He sat in the big chair long enough to know what it costs.
  [#8f3a2e] Take the seal. You sit in my place this year. / …And say half of what you think.

  [#8f3a2e] I know. I sat in it for twelve years. / Your uncle chairs it now. He’ll be kind to you. That’s worse. / Half, son. Half.
  [p] He promised his father half. He has never said half of anything. Next stop: Pyongyang, and a room full of men counting grain…!

### gusesa--high-summit  (High Summit, 634)
  person=gusesa look= from= place= scene=
  [p] He is not the first man this year to want to be king for all. He is the first to want it on a budget.
  [#c46b3a] Then the Southern Command takes the next levy. / Yushin’s banners have been testing the passes. If His Majesty wants Samhan, give me men — not speeches.
  [p] The north wants horses. The west wants timber and iron. Both want them from Central, and both say so twice.
  >>> CARD [card gusesa] The High Commander. He chairs the room like a feast and counts it like a granary.
  [#b2554a] (mild, as if chairing a feast) / Each front believes it is the only front. That is why we meet. / Eastern Command has kept the marches quiet. Let us not reward noise over results.
  [#d0362f] Quiet? / I have been killing tribes so this room can argue about who gets the horses. / Meanwhile the Second Emperor is not a tribute account. He is a man who murders brothers for a throne and then invents a reason.
  [#a83b34] Commander Yeon. Watch your tongue about foreign kings. / We have bought decades with gold. We will buy more — and spend the peace on Samhan.
  [#d0362f] You cannot buy a man who has already decided the price of your head. / I have watched how courts die. They starve the wall that is screaming, and fatten the wall that—

### samsin--high-summit  (High Summit, 634)
  person=samsin look= from= place= scene=Birth of Namseng
  [p] He reaches the house after midnight. One lamp, one midwife, and the mother. On the wall hangs a painting of Samsin, the birth goddess, prayed at so often that the paint has gone pale where the hands touch it.
  [#c4787a] Samsin… / This child alone — please. / …This time — please.
  [p] The painting does not stay paint. Samsin steps from the frame the way steam steps from a kettle, and lays a hand where mortal hands have failed.
  >>> CARD [card samsin] The birth goddess. She does not knock.
  [#c084a0] Do not weep. / I will open the breath. / The name — that is yours to give.
  [p] So the first heir arrives under Samsin's hand, the year of the Summit. They call him Namseng. Nobody wanted a poem in the name. It's the sound the room makes when the baby breathes.
  [#d0362f] Namseng. / …Heavier than it sounds. / This country. You will have to keep it.
  [p] He holds the boy up to the lamp and tells him the only bedtime story he knows: the one about the king who rode south and never counted grain.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Do not weep. / I will open the breath. / The name — that is yours to give."

### gwanggaeto--gwanggaeto-the-great-king  (Gwanggaeto, the Great King, 400)
  person=gwanggaeto look= from= place= scene=
  [p] Silla is drowning. An army from across the sea is inside its walls, and its king has one move left.
  >>> CARD [card gwanggaeto] Goguryeo’s widest king. The stele ran out of room before he ran out of fortresses.
  [quote] He was born big and imposing, with a will that would not be bridled.
  [scene] The Burning Capital
  [p] The Silla king stands on his own wall and counts the sea-raiders’ fires. There are more every night. Below, in the hall, his court is arguing about pride.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Servant. He wrote that word himself?"
    "Then they’ll come. Fifty thousand of them. / Tell him one thing more, so he hears it from me first. Servants don’t decide when the master’s horsemen go home."

### sadaham--sadaham  (Sadaham, 641, flashback 560)
  person=sadaham look= from= place= scene=
  [p] Back then the yard was new, and so was the idea. The king wanted boys who would ride ahead of the army and not ask why. The first year, he got a lot of them. Two of them got each other.

### seongchung--king-euija  (King Euija, 641)
  person=seongchung look= from= place= scene=
  [p] The white deer is the cheapest one. You take a young doe, you keep it out of the sun for a season, and you let it out on the hunting ground on a day the ministers are watching.
  [p] The stone at the Rock of Politics sweats before a good decision. It sweats because somebody rubs it with brine the night before, and the somebody is always the same man.
  [p] Rice comes up on ground where nothing was planted. Something was planted. It was planted at night.

### yunchung--yunchung  (Yunchung, 641)
  person=yunchung look= from= place= scene=
  [p] There was only one man Euija knew he could trust to deliver.

### kingsung--the-severing  (The Severing, 553–554)
  person=kingsung look= from= place= scene=
  [p] Two kings take a river back together: Seong of Baekje and the Cloud King of Silla. For a while their banners fly side by side. Then the Cloud King turns his army on Baekje’s half. He takes the river mouth and fills it with men who won’t ask what the alliance meant.
  [p] King Seong feels the cut in the marrow. He calls in everyone who still owes him: the last Gaya houses, a boatload of soldiers from the islands. Then he marches on the fortress that opens Silla's throat.
  >>> CARD [card kingsung] Baekje’s king. He has lost a river, and he means to get it back.
  [place gwansan]
  [p] For months the fight goes Baekje’s way. The crown prince holds the forward camp, half-starved; his men are boiling their saddle leather. One night his father rides out with fifty horse to steady him.
  [scene] The Night Road
  FIRST LINES:
    "Gaya…? / A prince of Geumgwan — on this road, tonight, why."
    "What. / A slave’s hand— no. A king’s head does not take a slave’s hand."
    "Every time I think of it… / It went into the marrow. / I cannot live on in disgrace."

### gumil--gumil  (Gumil, 642)
  person=gumil look= from= place=daeya scene=
  [place daeya]
  [p] The granary at Daeya can feed the garrison through a winter siege. Gumil knows the exact number of sacks. He counted them. Every tally he writes goes up the stair to a young man in a purple sleeve, who seals it without reading it.
  >>> CARD [card gumil] A yellow-sleeve officer. He does the work, and the purple sleeve signs it.
  [p] In Silla the sleeve tells you everything. Purple is True Bone, the old royal blood. Yellow is a man who will die at the rank he was born to. Nobody has to explain it twice. You can see it from across a yard.
  [scene] The Stair
  [p] This morning Gumil climbs the stair with the harvest tally and one more sheet under it. The second sheet is his. Four years of border pay, owed and never paid, added up to the last measure.
  [p] Pumsuk is twenty-four. He has held the fortress for a year, because his blood is right and his wife’s father is Chunchu. He is not a bad man. He is just a man who has never had to read the second sheet.
  FIRST LINES:
    "My pay, Commander. Four years of it. / The capital sends the rice. Somewhere between the capital and me, it gets eaten."
    "After the feast. / Putting a boy this green in charge of the border — does that make any sense?"
    "Ah, forgotten what country this is? To them we’re not even dirt~ / Say “True Bone” and the heavens part on their own~~"

### taizong--emperor  (Emperor, 643)
  person=taizong look= from= place=changan scene=

  [p] One character of that name nobody in this palace may write, because it belonged to the emperor’s late father. So a clerk wrote another one. The man in Pyongyang will be furious when he hears. That is a story for later.
  >>> CARD [card taizong] The Second Emperor of Tang. He owns half the world, and he is curious about the other half.
  [p] He has never lost a battle he led himself. He mentions this rarely, and only to people who already know.
  [scene] The Night Audience
  [card chusuiliang] The court diarist. He writes down everything the emperor says, which makes him the bravest man in the room.

    "It is noted, Majesty. As a joke."

### weizheng--four-dragons  (Four Dragons, 643)
  person=weizheng look= from= place= scene=The Sickroom
  [p] So the Second Emperor of the West is a man who has not heard another person say his own name since he was crowned, and there is nobody left alive who is allowed to.
  [scene] The Sickroom
  [p] The Imperial Minister is dying. At the foot of the bed the court diarist, Chu Suiliang, writes down everything the emperor says.
  >>> CARD [card weizheng] The emperor’s minister. His job is to say no, and he is very good at his job.
  [#9a7b4f] Your Majesty. When I am gone, there will be no one left to tell you no.
  [#c97a2e] Why else do you think I put up with you for twenty years.
  [#c97a2e] With bronze for a mirror, a man straightens his robes. / With history for a mirror, he sees the rise and fall of states. / With a man for a mirror, he sees his own faults. / …Today I lose one of my mirrors.

He’s riding to it anyway.
  [scene] Longmen Field
  [p] In a poor field at Longmen, a farmer named Xue Rengui is planning to rebury his ancestors. Millet, rammed earth, a hut that doesn’t pretend to be anything. He has the right soil for graves. He doesn’t yet know he has the wrong year for quiet.
  >>> CARD [card xuerengui] A poor farmer with good soil for graves. His wife thinks he could do better.
  [p] The cloth on his back is plain yellow peasant hemp, the cheapest dye the village still sells, the colour of millet at the wrong hour. He hoes. His wife, Liu, keeps the hut door.
  [p] The Son of Heaven is calling up troops for Liaodong. The edict reaches villages that have never seen a palace, and wives who have never left the furrow.
  [p] The edict comes on red paper, pasted to the well-house wall at the height of a man’s eyes: SERVE THE EMPEROR. Under it, in smaller characters, the quota. It does not ask for him by name. It asks for one man from every household with the right number of hands, and any man with hands will do.
  [#e8e3d5] The mounds… they’re not done. / Not the dirt. The hands. / The edict — I heard it. I did.
  FIRST LINES:

    "…Ancestors. Wait a little longer. / Until I come back carrying this ji. / The yellow clothes — I’ll leave them here."

### haemosu--haemosu  (Haemosu, -59)
  person=haemosu look= from= place=amnok scene=
  [p] Dawn, noon, dusk, night, always the same route. Below, the Amnok is a line he is not supposed to break: wet stone, morning shallows with no boat in them, rocks that are only rocks.
  [place amnok]
  [p] Haemosu, god of the sun, has kept this hour since before the river had daughters. Today the Amnok flashes under the wheel. He looks down, and the hour breaks.
  >>> CARD [card haemosu] The sun god. Punctual since before the rivers, until this afternoon.
  [p] In the shallows, three river-daughters are bathing: Yuhwa and her two sisters. Wet hair down their backs, the river at their hips. Nobody dressed for heaven. He falls in love and in lust in the same glance.
  [card yuhwa] The river’s youngest daughter, a nymph of the Amnok. Heaven is about to ruin her afternoon, or make it.
  [card hwahye] The eldest river-daughter. First into the water, every time.
  [card wihye] The middle sister. She laughs first and dives second.
  FIRST LINES:
    "…Stop. Stop the chariot."
    "Those thighs… / The water…"
    "Hey— / Wait. Hey. You. / Why aren’t you hiding? Look at me like that and I’m coming down."

### yuhwa--haemosu  (Haemosu, -59)
  person=yuhwa look= from= place=amnok scene=
  [p] Haemosu, god of the sun, has kept this hour since before the river had daughters. Today the Amnok flashes under the wheel. He looks down, and the hour breaks.
  [card haemosu] The sun god. Punctual since before the rivers, until this afternoon.
  [p] In the shallows, three river-daughters are bathing: Yuhwa and her two sisters. Wet hair down their backs, the river at their hips. Nobody dressed for heaven. He falls in love and in lust in the same glance.
  >>> CARD [card yuhwa] The river’s youngest daughter, a nymph of the Amnok. Heaven is about to ruin her afternoon, or make it.
  [card hwahye] The eldest river-daughter. First into the water, every time.
  [card wihye] The middle sister. She laughs first and dives second.
  [p] Hwahye and Wihye have left their silk on the rocks. The eldest folded hers once; the middle did not bother. Yuhwa’s ice-blue is still on her shoulder, wet.
  [p] Yuhwa kneels in the shallows with her hair in one fist like a dark rope and rinses the river out of it without hurrying. Heaven can wait on a rinse; she has decided that without saying it. With her back to the sky she looks over her shoulder, as if someone up there had said her name.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Unni. / Go. I’m here. / …I was going to say don’t look up."
    "Heaven looks down every day. / So today I’m supposed to blush? / …Come closer, if you want to see. / Into the water. / And decide… where your hands are going."
    "Come down first. / From the sky it’s an order. / At the water… I’ll hear it as a request. / Ask with your mouth… and I’ll answer with my name."

### jumong-exile--buyeo  (Buyeo, -40)
  person=jumong look=exile from= place= scene=The Egg
  [p] They name him Jumong, the good shot, because in those days people were named for what heaven had plainly already decided. He grows up with Geumwa’s sons, Daeso and Galsa.
  [p] They are boys first, three princes at one stake in one square, before anybody is an heir on purpose. They shoot with borrowed bows, too long in the arm.
  [p] Jumong can find a fly’s wing with an arrow before the bow fits his arm.
  >>> CARD [card jumong:exile] The best archer in Buyeo. The princes have noticed.
  [quote] His frame and face were striking and strange. At seven he was already unlike other children; he made his own bow and arrows, and of a hundred shots, a hundred hit. In the Buyeo tongue a good archer is
  [#e8563f] I’ll take the fly.
  [p] Daeso teaches the grip, then resents the hit. The lesson ends the moment the arrow is better than the teacher.
  [p] The yard hears the wood take it, a clean tick, and the praise does not arrive. Daeso keeps his hands on his own bow as if applause were a confession. Galsa looks at the dirt instead of the hit.
  FIRST LINES:
    "I’ll take the fly."
    "Then put the mark farther."
    "…How’d you know? / I didn’t tell anyone."

### haewonmek--buyeo  (Buyeo, -40)
  person=haewonmek look= from= place= scene=The Flight
  [p] Something keeps pace with him above the trees, black on black, going from branch to branch without seeming to hurry. A crow. He is too frightened to count its legs.
  [p] Jumong reaches the water alone, his death already written down for that day. No ford. No boat. The friends are a ridge away, on purpose.
  [p] Haewonmek, the reaper who collects each day’s dead, is already in the air. He skims the river toward him. Black hat, black silk, mouth bound shut. Jumong doesn’t see him. He’s looking at the water and the rain.
  >>> CARD [card haewonmek] A fetch of the underworld. Black hat, black silk, and a mouth bound shut so he can’t haggle.
  [p] A root takes his foot. He goes down on the wet stones, pine needles in his mouth, the bow a pace off as if it had been the first thing taken. Haewonmek crouches over him to collect what is owed, and the blow is already coming down.
  [p] The cloak arrives before the face. Rain fills it. A hand closes on Haewonmek’s wrist from behind, and the strike simply stops — the way an elder stops a sleeve that has gone too far.
  [p] Jumong’s cheek is in the mud. Haewonmek looks back. Behind him, in a dark hood, the sun god is holding his wrist and laughing, as if the night had grabbed the wrong man. The night is Haewonmek’s road. The joke is Haemosu’s.

  >>> CARD [card bidam:elder] First chair of the Harmony Council. Every vote now passes through his hands.
  [p] Under him sit the others, Yushin among them. They still decide only by unanimity. It’s the only way this council selects anything.
  [p] Then the room turns to the question everyone has been circling: when Her Majesty fails, who next. The Sacred Bone has thinned to one cousin. Someone says the name Princess Seungman the way you set a cup down that you expect everyone to drink from. She is forty-five, kind, careful with servants, and has never once surprised anybody.
  [p] One by one the hands go up. In a unanimous council a raised hand is a kind of weather — once it starts, it finishes. Yushin’s hand is among them. He has served one queen; he will serve her cousin.
  [p] Only one hand stays down.

  [p] Class 51’s first morning. Packed earth still dark. Bidam is sixteen. His father walks him as far as the yard gate and no further — Musan hall does not hover.
  >>> CARD [card sukwon] Bidam’s father. A man of few words, and he has saved them all for his son.
  [#3d4654] Bidam… / Do you know the meaning of your name.
  [#7b5cd6] Yes, father… / I was named after the Abhidharma, the higher teaching. It—
  [#3d4654] Yes… the higher teaching. / And as a young man, and as a Hwarang, your duty is to uphold that. / And remember this: / Even if no one else agrees with the truth… even if speaking it out loud causes others to defame and mock you… / You must always walk toward the truth, in isolation if you must. There
  [p] He does not name the Gaya-born boy who will share the class. He only ties Bidam’s headband once, tight, and lets the gate take him.

  [#7b5cd6] You heard right, Princess. One hand. Mine.
  [#9d7bd0] She can barely sit up, Bidam. The physicians say a season. Less. / Couldn’t you let her have one quiet winter?
  [#7b5cd6] I gave her thirteen quiet winters. I put her on the chair. / She was chosen because she was the cleverest. Now the room wants the nearest. / Forgive me, Princess. You are kind. Kindness does not hold a pass.

### yumjong--gi  (Gi (起), 645)
  person=yumjong look= from= place= scene=Yumjong
  [p] The guards look at their spears. Chunchu is across the sea. His orders, apparently, are not.
  [scene] Yumjong
  [p] Bidam does not recruit with speeches, whatever the Council thinks of him. He recruits with tea and long silences, and the first man to drink the tea is Yumjong, a True Bone whom nobody has ever accused of anything, because nobody has ever noticed him.
  >>> CARD [card yumjong] A quiet True Bone who drinks his tea slowly and listens fast.
  [undefined] The islands, now. Last summer it was the emperor’s war. / Your Lord Chunchu does get around.
  [undefined] Chunchu wants absolute power…!
  [undefined] What’s the difference between the West and the East anyway? / In both nations, their emperors cannot be removed by a vote. / Their people live as slaves.
  FIRST LINES:
    "The islands, now. Last summer it was the emperor’s war. / Your Lord Chunchu does get around."
    "And the Marshal?"
    "He’s not even Silla, you know. / Gaya. His great-grandfather handed over Geumgwan with the keys still warm. The men in the outer works would like hearing that."

### ibiga--suro  (Suro, 42)
  person=ibiga look= from= place= scene=
  [p] Before there is a Gaya, there is a ridge, and a sky god who looks at it too long.
  [p] Ibiga keeps the sky the way other gods keep a hall — cloud is his body, the living world a map he does not usually read. Then he looks down.
  >>> CARD [card ibiga] The sky god. Cloud is his body, and he does not usually look down.
  [p] On her mountain the Lady of the Right View is on watch. At first she is the ridge — jade stone, mist, a woman’s shape the mountain has not admitted yet. The mountain is a woman before it has a face. Then a face comes out of the stone. She is guarding the mountain as if it were a country. She does not look up. She does not need to. Then the sky occupies the path. Cloud comes down to the ridge.
  [card jeonggyeon] The mountain goddess. The ridge was a woman before anyone noticed.
  [#1e4d9c] That ridge… / That woman. / I have flown this path a thousand times. Why is the mountain looking back.
  [p] Love arrives as weather — sudden, unasked. He cannot keep the hour. He falls before he lands. The sky comes down to touch the mountain, and does not leave.
  FIRST LINES:
    "That ridge… / That woman. / I have flown this path a thousand times. Why is the mountain looking back."
    "Mountain. / Your shoulder… is warmer than cloud. / Your waist… steeper than cliff."
    "To touch. / I looked… and could not hold back. / The knees… already are."

### suro--suro  (Suro, 42)
  person=suro look= from= place= scene=
  [p] He holds her with one arm. The other is cloud. The ridge is still a mountain; the mountain is still a woman. She does not look up. She does not have to.
  [p] By morning the ridge remembers two gods who would not let go. From that heat come eggs, and from the eggs, kings.
  [p] Their eggs fall to earth on a hill called Guji, and wait for someone to sing.
  >>> CARD [card suro] King Suro. Born from a golden egg, and in no hurry to marry anyone local.
  [quote] He stood nine feet tall, like Tang of Yin. His face was a dragon’s, like the High Ancestor of Han. His eyebrows shone in eight colours, like Yao. His eyes had double pupils, like Shun.
  [scene] Mount Guji
  [p] On Earth, the people sing a song to call for a new king.
  [quote] Turtle, turtle — show your head. If you do not, we will roast and eat you.
  FIRST LINES:
    "… / ……You. / Your mouth…"
    "Your waist… / I mustn’t… / If I touch…"
    "…Hungry… / I can’t… speak…"

### heohwangok--suro  (Suro, 42)
  person=heohwangok look= from= place=geumgwan scene=The Red Sail
  [place geumgwan]
  [scene] The Red Sail
  [p] Queen Heo, an Indian princess, becomes the first queen of Golden Gaya.
  >>> CARD [card heohwangok] Heo Hwang-ok. She sailed farther than anyone in Samhan had heard of, and arrived dressed for it.
  [p] She arrives on a red-sailed ship at twenty-one — foreign, luminous, built like nowhere on this coast. The beach is only a door. The first time Suro falls in love is not on the sand.
  [p] In the timber court of Golden Gaya she presents herself — no servant speaking for her, her own name, silk that does not belong to this hall. He is already on the dais. He meant to receive a princess. He receives a woman, and love hits him before protocol can stand up.
  [p] Protocol is still trying to stand. He is already off the dais. He comes down with one arm — gold around violet, the same hold the sky used on the ridge, only this time the hall has columns and a floor.
  [p] Servants had been sent to the ship. She refused them. So the court is where they meet — and the moment he sees her, speech leaves him like heat from an open kiln.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Have you come to fetch me… / or have you already begun to take me. / With your eyes. / Your mouth… looks dry."
    "Yes. / My mouth. / When the king looks at me like that… I get warmer. / Your hands… where do you mean to put them. / Even if you can’t speak — your hands know."
    "Then touch. / Since the king can’t choose… I’ll choose for you. / Here. / And here. / You’re shaking."

### jinduk-queen--queen-jinduk  (Queen Jinduk, 647)
  person=jinduk look=queen from=princess place= scene=
  [p] The crown was made for her cousin and has to be padded at the temples. Seungman sits very still while the goldsmith does it, because somebody told her once that Dukman never fidgeted, and she has believed it for forty years.
  [p] Seungman is crowned Queen Jinduk before the blood on the yard dries. The bloodline’s last polite miracle, stamped and filed while the censers are still warm. The succession Bidam died objecting to passes at last. Unanimously.
  [quote] Taizong* of Tang sent an envoy bearing his tally to confer on the late queen the posthumous rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and to invest the new queen as Pillar of State and King of Lelan
  >>> CARD [card jinduk:queen]
  [quote] Seungman was full-figured and beautiful, seven feet tall, and her hands hung down past her knees.
  [p] Alchun is not at the coronation. The court writes his absence down as illness. Everyone knows the illness’s name. It lasted ten days.
  [p] The court does not mean to compare. It simply cannot stop. The old Queen read the peony seeds before they were planted. She heard frogs at Jade Gate Pond in midwinter and sent two thousand men to the exact valley where five hundred Baekje soldiers were hiding. She named the day of her own death and was right about it. The new Queen is gentle, and good at a loom, and has never once predicted anything.
  [#c9a0a8] The old Queen would have known it was going to rain. / Shh. / …She would have, though.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Yushin… preserve the sacred country…"
    "Bidam…"
    "Yushin… surely Bidam’s words are not weighing on you…?"

### gaozong-prince--huangdi  (Huangdi (皇帝), 648)
  person=gaozong look=prince from= place= scene=The Gyuku Ground
  [p] The emperor shakes his head, still smiling, and goes back to his memorials. Chunchu says nothing more. He is watching the brush in the emperor’s hand: one man, one brush, and at the far end of it a province three months away. Nobody in this palace will ever meet in a room to vote that hand off the paper. He cannot stop looking at it, the way a poor man looks at a jade he will never afford, and he does not let one par
  [scene] The Gyuku Ground
  [p] The days between audiences belong to someone else. The crown prince — Li Zhi, twenty years old and still allowed to laugh with his shoulders — steals Chunchu from the memorial-hall the way a younger brother steals an older one from a funeral, and takes him to the imperial gyuku ground.
  >>> CARD [card gaozong:prince] Li Zhi. Heir to everything, and the first man in Chang’an to laugh.
  [p] They play gyuku until the dust makes them the same colour. Li Zhi talks like a man who has waited his whole life to be ordinary with somebody dangerous. Chunchu lets him.
  [#b8935a] When I am emperor — / No. That sounds like a curse. When the years have been kinder — / I will still want this. A friend who does not need my title to stand upright.
  [#D8258C] Then keep me as I am. / When you are emperor I will still be a man from a small country with a large grudge. / That is the only honest introduction I have.
  [#b8935a] Good. / Brothers, then — of the inconvenient kind.
  FIRST LINES:

    "(calling from behind) Wu! You haven’t been scaring our guests away, have you?"

  person=wuzetian look=consort from= place= scene=The Farewell Banquet
  [#c97a2e] Zhi — keep this one. Men who can rhyme on their knees are rarer than honest generals.
  [p] Twenty characters. He has asked for an army, flattered an emperor out of his own classics, and called his neighbours a bad wind, without one word anybody could quote back at him.
  [p] Behind the screen Wu does not merely listen. She works the room without entering it: a glance that steadies a nervous maid, a smile that slows a minister’s cup, a silence that turns every eye in the hall back to the foreign prince.
  >>> CARD [card wuzetian:consort] Wu, a lady of the inner palace. The screen is doing very little of the hiding.
  [scene] The Lodging
  [p] On the morning before he is to leave, a parcel comes to the lodging from the palace. Inside are rubbings of two steles in the emperor’s own hand, and a new history of the Jin dynasty, so fresh from the Historiography Office that the paste on the bindings is still soft.

  [#D8258C] Fresh. Here they harmonize it before the paste dries. / Read it slowly anyway. We’ll want to know what the Jin are allowed to have done.
  FIRST LINES:

    "Chunchu… you are the one from the country with the woman king, correct?"

### jukji--royal-secretariat  (Royal Secretariat, 651)
  person=jukji look= from= place= scene=
  [#D8258C] We call it the Royal Secretariat.
  [#D8258C] Today, Silla reinvents the court.
  [p] Nobody laughs. The youngest clerk writes the name down as if the words had always been waiting for ink. Outside, the Harmony Council is still debating the same petition. Inside, the petition has somewhere to land.
  >>> CARD [card jukji] A Hwarang who sailed with Chunchu to Chang’an and wrote down everything. Quiet, exact, and always holding the right paper.
  [#6a9e7a] Petition. Seal. Courier. / I can do that before the Council finishes clearing its throat.
  [#D8258C] Then you are its Premier. The Secretariat is yours. / You’re young, you’re quick, and you already write faster than the Council talks. / In Chang’an the emperor does not wait for every uncle to agree. I watched that power and wanted it for this country — not for my vanity. For speed.
  [p] The Council finds out in the third week. Alchun is High Councillor now, because after Bidam nobody else wanted the chair. He comes to the side hall himself, with the border petition under his arm. He has been meaning to debate it.
  [#8fb3e0] Oi. This petition. / We were going to argue about it at the full moon.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Petition. Seal. Courier. / I can do that before the Council finishes clearing its throat."
    "It’s sealed, my lord. The garrison marched yesterday."
    "The Council asked what my title means. / I told them: 侍中 — I stand beside the work. / They did not laugh. That was how I knew it had worked."

### gaozong-emperor--jiabeng  (Jiabeng (駕崩), 649)
  person=gaozong look=emperor from=prince place= scene=The Cuiwei Palace
  [p] Someone touches his elbow. Someone else is already writing. The empire does not wait for grief to finish its sentence.
  [p] The court kneels, and the young man rises — the same hands that would not leave the bed now accepting the seal, the edict, the yellow silk that means the West has a new centre.
  [#b8935a] I receive the late emperor’s last command. / From this day—— / ……We will listen.
  >>> CARD [card gaozong:emperor]
  [p] He does not say I. He says the word that empties a man of his own name. The hall answers like a single throat.
  [p] The will is long on mourning and short on everything else, except one line, which the new emperor reads twice. The war in Liaodong is to stop.
  [p] The great emperor is given a temple name — Taizong. The clerks write it in the register and close the book.
  [quote] Eighth year, summer, fourth month: Taizong* of Tang died. His testamentary edict called off the Liaodong campaign.
  FIRST LINES:

### jayi--jahee  (Jahee, 644)
  person=jayi look= from= place=danghang scene=
  [place danghang]
  [p] Seonpum has a daughter who keeps his inkstones. Her name is Jahee. She has watched the prince for three days, and she has already decided his arithmetic is sloppy.
  >>> CARD [card jayi] A harbour girl who counts faster than the customs men.
  [#e8a0bf] Your sums are wrong. / The tide does not care that you are a prince. / Count again. / While I am watching.
  [#C41E3A] …Where. / No — / Please show me.
  [p] She corrects the sum with her father’s good brush. She is not supposed to touch it. She took it off his desk an hour ago, because it is the only one that writes small enough. He watches her mouth instead of the numbers, and she lets him, once.
  [p] Then a rider comes down the coast road with a letter from Yushin. The army is marching west, against seven Baekje forts. The grain sails on the morning tide. Bupmin is to sail with it.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Your sums are wrong. / The tide does not care that you are a prince. / Count again. / While I am watching."
    "It won’t. You’re forty sacks short, somewhere between the third ship and the fifth. / Forty sacks is a company that doesn’t eat for a week."
    "…That’s my father coughing. / He only coughs like that when he’s pretending not to be there. / …Which is why it has to be now. / Before the tide comes in."

### hyukgose--hyukgose  (Hyukgose, -57)
  person=hyukgose look= from= place= scene=
  [#5a8fc4] It’s a gourd. We dug up a gourd with a baby in it.
  [#7a9e6b] Then that’s his name. Park. Gourd.
  [p] They call him Park, for the gourd, and Hyukgose, to rule with brightness. Then six practical men look at each other and crown him king while he is still a boy. A boy, they reason, cannot have taken sides yet.
  >>> CARD [card hyukgose] Hyukgose. Born from an egg, crowned before his voice broke.
  [quote] They bathed him in the eastern spring. His body gave off light, the birds and beasts danced together, heaven and earth shook, and the sun and moon turned clear and bright.
  [scene] Alyeong Well
  [p] A few years later, at Alyeongjeong well, a dragon with a chicken’s head leaves a girl behind. She has a beak where her lips should be, until they wash her in the north stream and it falls off. They name her Alyoung, after the well.

### talhae--talhae  (Talhae, -19)
  person=talhae look= from= place= scene=
  [p] It has come a long way. A thousand li north-east of Wa, the islands across the sea, the queen of a country called Dapana carried a child for seven years and was delivered of an egg. The king said a person who lays an egg is an ill omen and should get rid of it. She could not. She wrapped it in silk, packed it in a chest with treasure, and gave it to the sea.
  [p] It reaches Gaya first. The people of Golden Gaya see a strange chest bobbing off their beach and, being sensible, leave it there.
  [p] Gaya tells it differently, and with more nerve. In the Gaya chronicle Talhae comes ashore a grown man, walks into King Suro’s hall, and asks for the throne.
  >>> CARD [card talhae] Seok Talhae. He arrived in a chest and talks like he owns the beach.
  [quote] He stood nine feet tall, fine and bright in bearing, and cleverer than other men.
  [#5a7fa8] I’ve come for your throne. / You can fight me for it, or you can save us both the afternoon.
  [#8B5CF6] …Heaven gave it to me. / I— it isn’t mine to give. Or to… lose.
  [p] So they fight the way kings fight in that country. Talhae becomes a hawk, and Suro becomes an eagle. Talhae becomes a sparrow, and Suro becomes a falcon. When Talhae is a man again he is standing in the middle of the hall with feathers on his shoulders, and he bows.
  FIRST LINES:
    "I’ve come for your throne. / You can fight me for it, or you can save us both the afternoon."
    "…That was a falcon. / Fine. I’ll find a country with a smaller king."
    "No. / Is this the country?"

### heavenearthking--heaven-earth-king  (Heaven–Earth King, 태초)
  person=heavenearthking look= from= place= scene=Two Suns
  [scene] Two Suns
  [p] In the beginning there were two suns and two moons. By day people dropped in the fields with their hoes still in their hands; by night they froze in their own doorways. Nobody ever had a decent night’s sleep or a decent harvest, and the old died faster than anyone could bury them.
  [p] Above all of it sat Heaven–Earth King, who ran the living and the dead out of one office and therefore never went home. One night he fell asleep at the desk anyway, and dreamed he was eating: one sun, one moon, swallowed whole, one of each.
  >>> CARD [card heavenearthking] The god with two jobs and one desk. He dreams about breakfast.
  [#C30000] ……Huh. / One each. / I ate one of each. / Ha— that’s a son. Someone’s going to shoot those down.
  [p] He comes down to the world to find the mother of that dream, and finds her in the poorest house on the road: a girl the village calls the Lady of Wisdom, a hearth with no fire in it, and a rice jar she does not open in front of guests.
  [#c9b18f] Who are you.
  [#C30000] Someone passing. / A hungry one.
  FIRST LINES:
    "……Huh. / One each. / I ate one of each. / Ha— that’s a son. Someone’s going to shoot those down."
    "Someone passing. / A hungry one."
    "…… / Your rice has a bit of bite to it."

  [p] It drifted for years and washed up in a foreign country, and the boy came out of it a warrior, and won that country’s wars, and married its princess. And then he came home.

### chunbok--coup  (Coup, 657)
  person=chunbok look= from= place= scene=
  [p] Euija names forty-one of his own sons to the Assembly, firing every single existing member. Eight houses spent four generations sharpening tricks on each other. Marriages. Roads. Clerks planted in rival counting-rooms. In one morning the king clears the board. He simply changes the pieces. By noon nobody has an answer.
  [p] Satek Chunbok is named Premier. His own clan watches him walk to the chair. The Enabling Law did not abolish the chair. It only changed who sits in it.
  >>> CARD [card chunbok] A Satek in the Satek chair, sitting for the king.
  [p] Forty-one sons need forty-one seats. None goes to the Ye family. They have held Bear Fortress for four generations and never once been asked to court. Ye Sikjin reads the list at home, twice. Then he puts it in a drawer.
  [place ungjin]
  [p] Then he hands out the quiet money that really runs Baekje. Harbour warehouses. River pilot fees. The stamp a ship needs before it sails east. The martial law was the noise. The stamps are what change.
  [p] He cannot do what Yeon did. Baekje would not forgive it, and more to the point, he would not. He does not need a banquet. He needs a majority that looks like kinship.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Your Majesty… as Your Majesty well knows, the houses are counting tonight. / If a boat leaves for Tamla before the benches are cold, they will read it as war. / Let them get used to losing first. A month. Then send for him."
    "Do not trouble yourself over Baekje."
    "Baekje will fall on its own. / Where blood ties are strong, the state grows weak. / The Baekje clans love a family feud — they will envy each other into ruin."

    "My son is only sixteen, but his spirit is brave enough. / In today’s battle — can he be the mark the three armies aim by?"

### munmu-king--kim-chunchu  (Kim Chunchu†, 661)

### liurengui--ungjin-commandery  (Ungjin Commandery, 661)
  person=liurengui look= from= place= scene=The Black Tortoise
  [scene] The Black Tortoise
  [p] Someone has to hold what the Tang broke. Nobody in Chang’an expected to see Liu Rengui in uniform again. He is sixty. Last year he lost a grain fleet in a storm and was stripped of office. Now he comes east as a commoner in white, to earn it back. In his baggage: the Tang calendar, and the list of names nobody may write.
  >>> CARD [card liurengui] The Black Tortoise. Sixty, disgraced last year, and in an excellent mood.
  [#1f2937] Heaven means to make an old man rich, it seems. / Send me the calendar for this country, and the list of names one must not write. If we are going to sweep the east clean, the east should at least know what year it is.
  [p] Between skirmishes the Black Tortoise does what he actually came for, which is paperwork. He counts the households of Baekje village by village and writes them down as numbers. He mends dykes and bridges. He posts the Tang calendar at every crossroads, with the list of names that may not be written, so that the people of Baekje will know which characters to leave out of their letters home.
  [#1f2937] A village that knows what year it is pays its tax on time. / Put one up at the ferry as well. People read while they wait for the boat.
  [scene] The Ferry
  FIRST LINES:
    "Heaven means to make an old man rich, it seems. / Send me the calendar for this country, and the list of names one must not write. If we are going to sweep the east clean, the east should at least know what year it is."
    "A village that knows what year it is pays its tax on time. / Put one up at the ferry as well. People read while they wait for the boat."
    "Read it to me first."

### saimei--king-pungjang  (King Pungjang, 661, flashback 660)

  [undefined] Before anyone asks him anything, Mother, I will. / Prince. Do they want you, or your name?
  [#e6c76a] …Both, I expect. The name first. / I am still a son of Baekje. I have only… forgotten some of the words.
  [p] The empress has let all of it run: her son’s arithmetic, the admiral’s hat, the prince’s missing words. Then she speaks once.
  >>> CARD [card saimei] The Eastern Empress. She has outlived two reigns and most of her ministers’ opinions.
  [#c0504d] My son wants to know what we owe Baekje. / Bring him the sword. The one with seven branches.
  [p] Three hundred years ago a Baekje king sent the King of Wa a sword with seven branches. It was a gift. It was also a message.
  [p] It is iron, two and a half feet long, with six branches off a central blade and sixty-one characters inlaid in gold down both sides. It has never been sharpened. It was never going to be.
  [p] The inscription is the interesting part, because the two countries have spent fifteen hundred years disagreeing about a single verb: whether Baekje presented it upward, or bestowed it downward.
  FIRST LINES:
    "My son wants to know what we owe Baekje. / Bring him the sword. The one with seven branches."
    "Asking for soldiers is old. Holding up a falling house is older. / The sea is also a border, my son. When the western roof catches, our eaves are next. / Give them the ships. Give the boy a cap of rank and a wife, so he does not arrive look"

### hwanin--dangun-old-joseon  (Dangun & Old Joseon, Long ago)
  person=hwanin look= from= place= scene=
  [p] Before there are any kingdoms, there is a son in heaven who keeps looking down. He is Hwanung. His father Hwanin, the Lord of Heaven, notices, looks down himself at a mountain called Taebaek and the people living around it, and decides the world could use his son.
  >>> CARD [card hwanin] The Lord of Heaven. He has been watching this peninsula since before it had names.
  [p] Hwanin does not plough — he opens the sky. Three seals go down with his son, so that nobody on the ground can mistake him for a prince playing at exile. Every later king in this chronicle will cut seals of his own, and every one of them is copying these.
  [p] Hwanung lands on a mountain under the sacred birch. He names the ground beneath it the Divine City. Three thousand followers come down with him. Among them are the lords of wind, rain and cloud. Someone has to argue with the weather.
  [card hwanung] Hwanung. A son of heaven who kept looking down until his father let him go.
  FIRST LINES: (none)

### hwanung--dangun-old-joseon  (Dangun & Old Joseon, Long ago)
  person=hwanung look= from= place= scene=
  [p] Hwanin does not plough — he opens the sky. Three seals go down with his son, so that nobody on the ground can mistake him for a prince playing at exile. Every later king in this chronicle will cut seals of his own, and every one of them is copying these.
  [p] Hwanung lands on a mountain under the sacred birch. He names the ground beneath it the Divine City. Three thousand followers come down with him. Among them are the lords of wind, rain and cloud. Someone has to argue with the weather.
  >>> CARD [card hwanung] Hwanung. A son of heaven who kept looking down until his father let him go.
  [p] From there he hands out civilisation in instalments. Laws. Punishments. Lifespans. Illness. Good and evil. Medicine. Three hundred and sixty matters in all. Somebody counted.
  [p] There is a short way to tell the rest, the way it is carved on stones. The long way begins, as long ways do, with a bear who wanted something so badly that she outlasted a tiger for it.
  [p] A bear and a tiger come to him and ask to be made human. He gives them a bundle of mugwort, twenty cloves of garlic, and one instruction: stay out of the sun for a hundred days.
  [scene] The Sacred Birch
  FIRST LINES:
    "…Not today."
    "I saw you. / The garlic reached this far."
    "Too late. / Stay. I mean— don't go. Your hand—"

### ungnyeo--dangun-old-joseon  (Dangun & Old Joseon, Long ago)
  person=ungnyeo look= from= place= scene=The Sacred Birch
  [p] A bear and a tiger come to him and ask to be made human. He gives them a bundle of mugwort, twenty cloves of garlic, and one instruction: stay out of the sun for a hundred days.
  [scene] The Sacred Birch
  [p] The bear stays. She comes out a woman on the twenty-first morning, garlic still on her breath, and finds the mountain already staffed — wind, rain, cloud, and not one of them a husband. So she stands under the sacred tree. Not once. Every day, on the path he has to take if he means to reach the hall.
  >>> CARD [card ungnyeo] Ungnyeo. Twenty-one days in a cave, and the tiger left first. A husband should be easy.
  [p] He means to reach the hall. On the third evening he gets as far as the birch, and the seal in his hand becomes a thing he is holding for no reason he can name.
  [#c9b18f] You're going to walk past again.
  [#d4b86a] …Not today.
  [#c9b18f] Yesterday you did. / And the day before. I was standing right here.

### dangun--dangun-old-joseon  (Dangun & Old Joseon, Long ago)
  person=dangun look= from= place= scene=Asadal
  [#c9b18f] Marry me in the morning. / Right now I'm here.
  [scene] Asadal
  [p] Their son is Dangun. The name on the stone is Wanggeom: a king who governs, not one who inherits a bone rank. He founds Asadal where the mountain meets the plain. He rules for fifteen hundred years, and then he becomes the mountain.
  >>> CARD [card dangun] Dangun. Half heaven, half bear, and all the paperwork of a first king.
  [quote] He granted three heavenly seals and sent him to govern. Hwanung led a following of three thousand and descended under the sacred altar-tree on the summit of Mount Taebaek; this was called the Divine C
  [place asadal]
  [p] Every later crown in these kingdoms argues, one way or another, back to the woman who used to be a bear. Her son’s city keeps his name long after he has become a mountain.
  [scene] The Fall of Joseon
  FIRST LINES: (none)

### daejoyoung--balhae  (Balhae, 698)
  person=daejoyoung look= from= place= scene=
  [p] The winter after Pyongyang falls, the mountains of Manchuria do not care who won. Snow comes to the knee, then to the thigh, and the wind off the ridges finds every seam a coat has. Gulgul walks in front, bent under a leather pack and wrapped in so much fur he looks like something the forest would hunt. His son walks in his tracks, because there are no other tracks.
  [p] In the pack, under dried millet and a spare pair of boots, wrapped in a strip of red silk, rides a piece of the Goguryeo crown no longer than a finger: one gold branch snapped off when the palace fell, its little leaves still hanging on their wires. Nobody else would carry it north. Behind them is the smoke of someone else’s victory. Ahead is only the cold that Yeon once pulled a Mohe boy out of.
  >>> CARD [card daejoyoung] Dae Joyoung. A boy with frozen feet, and a piece of a crown in the pack.
  [#c45a4a] Father… / Father, my feet… I can’t feel my feet.
  [#8b3a3a] Good. / Better than feeling them.
  [#c45a4a] What kind of— Father!
  [#8b3a3a] There. Under the rock. / A little more.
  FIRST LINES:
    "Father… / Father, my feet… I can’t feel my feet."
    "What kind of— Father!"
    "Father. What’s… that? / The shiny thing. That. / Is that gold? We had gold? Then why is it always millet gruel—"
